reason: Quotes state IPv4 support cannot be disabled for the VPC and subnets, and that the VPC can operate in dual-stack mode with IPv4 and IPv6 independent.
Quote states a VPC must have an IPv4 CIDR block and can optionally have more IPv4 blocks and one or more IPv6 blocks.
Quote under IPv4 VPC CIDR blocks gives the allowed size between /16 (65,536) and /28 (16).
Step 1 row of the steps table says associate an Amazon-provided or BYOIP IPv6 CIDR block with the VPC and subnets.
Step 2 row gives the public subnet route to the internet gateway and the private subnet route to an egress-only internet gateway.
Step 3 row covers IPv6 security group rules and IPv6 rules for custom network ACL rules.
Step 4 row says assign IPv6 addresses to instances from the subnet's IPv6 range.
Quote states IPv6 addresses are globally unique and public by default, and the egress-only internet gateway gives outbound-only access.
The /44 to /60 quote sits under the IPAM pool option only; nothing quoted gives that range for a BYOIP (IPv6 CIDR owned by me) block, so the BYOIP part of the claim is unsupported.
Quote states Amazon-provided IPv6 addresses are always advertised, globally unique and reachable, with reachability controlled by routing, security groups and network ACLs.
Quotes state the automatic IPv6 outbound security group rule unless original outbound rules were modified, and automatic IPv6 rules on an unmodified default network ACL.
Quotes state you can request a block from Amazon's pool and, for the Amazon-provided block, cannot choose the range yourself; claim keeps that scope.

Quotes give sizes and 'up to five' but say nothing about adjustability, yet the qualifier says adjustable true; the quota table (amazon-vpc-limits) shows 5 is an adjustable default (up to 50), so 'up to 5' as a hard max needs the quota row as evidence.
Verbatim match with the quote under Considerations.
Quotes and context state IPv6 does not fragment in the network, the oversized packet is dropped and ICMPv6 Packet Too Big (Type 2) is returned.
Quote says the link-local addresses are used to communicate with services available only in the VPC; the claim adds 'used only to', an absolute the quote does not state.
Both quotes match the claim: VPC supports IPv6-only subnets and EC2 launches Nitro-based instances into them.
Verbatim match with the note under Step 2.
Document history gives three router addresses from November 11, 2022; subnet sizing lists ::1 plus the FE80::/10 EUI-64 address and FE80:ec2::1.
Quote states IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR blocks are treated separately and a ::/0 route is needed for IPv6.
Table row reads Yes, No, Yes, No under the header columns as claimed.
Quotes give the isolated subnet definition and that subnet type is determined by routing configuration.
Quote says the web server rules allow HTTP and HTTPS from the load balancer; the claim's 'only from the load balancer' is an absolute the quote does not state.
Quotes cover the local route in every table, one per IPv4 CIDR block, and the automatic IPv6 local route.
Quotes state no VPC endpoints in Local Zone subnets and provisioned IPs cannot move between the Local Zone and the parent Region.
Three quotes match the three parts of the claim.
Quotes and context state the automatic main route table, that routes can be changed, that it cannot be deleted, and the local-only default for a nondefault VPC.
Quote and its example (S3 prefix list to a gateway endpoint, peer CIDR to a peering connection) support more specific routes to avoid NAT gateway processing charges and route traffic privately.
Quotes state all EC2 instance types support 1500 MTU, the largest Ethernet packet size over most of the internet, and the maximum depends on instance type.
Quotes state fragmentation or drop with Don't Fragment, and caution with jumbo frames for traffic leaving the VPC.
Near-verbatim match with the whitepaper sentence.
Quotes and context state each network ACL has asterisk inbound and outbound rules that deny unmatched packets, and they cannot be deleted.
Quotes state the backup-layer role and the SSH-from-anywhere example exactly.
Both limitation bullets match the claim.
Quotes state changes apply automatically to associated subnets and take effect after a short period.
Quote and its bullet give the lower-number deny rule inside a wide allowed range.
Quote states the deny rule with source 0.0.0.0/0 or the subnet CIDR stops load balancer health checks.
Quotes state the client chooses the range by operating system and many Linux kernels including Amazon Linux use 32768-61000.
Three quotes give 1024-65535 for NAT gateway, ELB and Lambda; the return-traffic rule follows from the ephemeral-port rules in the same context.
Quote states opening 1024-65535 for public-facing instances with deny rules for malicious ports placed earlier.
